steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The exposure triangle: aperture (f-stop), shutter speed and ISO work together — changing one affects the others.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Aperture controls depth of field: wide aperture (f/1.8) = shallow DoF; narrow aperture (f/16) = deep DoF.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Shutter speed controls motion: fast (1/1000s) freezes action; slow (1/15s) creates blur and sense of movement.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: ISO controls sensor sensitivity: low ISO (100) = clean image; high ISO (3200+) = noisy/grainy but usable in low light.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring camera controls and exposure. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with camera controls and exposure. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with camera controls and exposure. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to camera controls and exposure, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined out | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
